(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Mr. Rachakonda Ramakrishna, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Mujib Kumar Sadasivuni, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the respondents.

2. This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of Habeas Corpus declaring the order of detention dated 15.10.2022 passed by respondent No.2 and the consequential confirmation order by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.2247, dated 01.12.2022 as illegal and to set aside the same and for a consequential direction to release the detenu, Mr. Murthuja Ali @ Damar, S/o Babar Ali.
3.

Respondent No.2 passed the detention order dated 15.10.2022 under the provisions of Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders,
Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities KL,J & PSS,J Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders,

5. In the detention order, there is reference with regard to the involvement of the detenu in seventy five (75) property offences under different Police Stations of the States of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu,
Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana during the years from KL,J & PSS,J 2005 to 2015.
In the year 2016 also, detention order was issued by Hyderabad Police Commissionerate and he was detained in Central Prison at Cherlapally.
After serving detention period, he was released from the Jail in July, 2021.

Despite the same, he did not mend his attitude and again involved in the aforesaid four (04) cases apart from Crime No.589 of 2022 of Medipally Police Station registered for the offence punishable under Section - 379 of IPC with regard to theft of parked motorcycle.
After having come to the subjective satisfaction only, the detaining authority passed the impugned detention order.

6. As per the contents of the order of detention and the counter affidavit filed by respondent No.2,
the grounds for passing the order of detention are that the detenu has been repeatedly indulging in the acts of 'goondaism' by committing property offences i.e., chain snatchings in an organized way and creating terror and a feeling of insecurity among the public especially women folks which disturbs peace and tranquility in the ear and acted in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
7. Perusal of the record would reveal that the detenu committed the aforesaid four (04) crimes apart from Crime No.589 of 2022 of Medipally Police Station during the year 2022.
Earlier, the detenu also KL,J & PSS,J involved in 75 property offences under different police station limits in the aforementioned States.
According to the respondent authorities, earlier also P.D. Act was imposed on the detenu and he was sent to Central Prison, Cherlapally.

After his release in the month of July,
2021, there was no change in his attitude and continues in commission of similar offences.
Therefore, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences which would disturb the public order, respondent No.2 issued the impugned detention order dated 15.10.2022.
The same was confirmed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.2247, dated 01.12.2022.

8. Mr. Rachakonda Ramakrishna, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that though the aforesaid four (04) crimes were referred and relied on by the detaining authority for passing order of detention, the same can be dealt with by ordinary law by the competent Criminal Courts instead of passing impugned detention order.
He would further submit that the offences alleged to have committed by the detenu come under the ambit of law and order and the same are against particular individual.
Further, the crimes were registered against the detenu based on confessions.
The detaining authority passed the order of detention on flimsy grounds without any basis in a mechanical manner.

There are no material to substantiate and justify for treating the detenu as KL,J Murthuja Ali Alias Damar vs The State Of Telengana on 4 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126857507/

sentences.text: Therefore, he sought to set aside the impugned detention order and the consequential confirmation order.

9. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious in nature, as he is a 'habitual offender' in many chain snatching cases and other serious offences in various States, the details of which are mentioned in the counter affidavit.
In Crime No.428 of 2022 of KPHB Police Station, the detenu while committing the offence of chain snatching made an attempt to kill the victim.
Considering the seriousness of offences, the Court below rejected the bail petition filed by the detenu twice and this Court once.

The detaining authority, considering the entire material available on record and after arriving at the subjective satisfaction only passed the detention order in order to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences.
The said detention order was confirmed by respondent No.1.
There is no error in it.

sentences.text: As discussed above, though the detaining authority referred to about the involvement of the detenu in 75 crimes during the years 2005 to 2015 and Crime No.589 of 2022, he has relied upon the four (04) crimes/cases mentioned in the above said table and issued the impugned detention order.

All the said four crimes are relating to chain snatchings within the jurisdiction of respondent No.2.
11.

It is relevant to note that from out of the said four crimes, the detenu did not move bail applications in three crimes mentioned at serial Nos.2 to 4 of the above table and bail applications filed in Crime No.428 of 2022 were dismissed by the Court below twice and this Court once on 28.09.2022 in Crl.P. No.8626 of 2022.
PT warrants were issued against him in the said three crimes.
The offences registered against the detenu are punishable under Sections - 392, 307 and 393 of IPC.
He was involved in 75 crimes earlier.
Thus, according to the respondents, the case of the detenu falls under the category of 'Goonda'.

Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of Act, 1986 defines "Goonda", which means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang,
habitually .

sentences.text: 12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration3 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society.
The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing.

13. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar4, the Apex Court held as under:

sentences.text: "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some?
The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must .
AIR 1966 SC 740 KL,J & PSS,J affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.
A District Magistrate is entitled to take action under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances.

It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order"
also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order".
One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State.

It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State."
14.

In Mallada K. Sri Ram v. The State of Telangana5, the Apex Court considering the fact that only two (02) crimes were registered against the detenu and he was granted bail on imposition of certain conditions, and there was no disturbance to the public order, set aside the detention order.

sentences.text: 15. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar6, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean .

(1984) 3 SCC 14 KL,J & PSS,J 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission
would not characterize as an act of 'habitual'.

The Apex Court was of the opinion that to qualify as a 'habit', a person must have grown accustomed to leading a life of crime, whereby it would be a force of habit,
inherent or latent, in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him as dangerous to society in general.

16. Thus, the detaining authority while invoking the powers under the Act No.1 of 1986, has to consider the entire material on record and come to a subjective satisfaction that due to the acts committed by the detenu, nature of offences and the manner in which the same were committed would disturb the public order.
To prevent the detenu from committing the similar offences, the detaining authority shall issue preventive detention order against the detenu.

sentences.text: There is no dispute with regard to the legal proposition that the detention order shall be issued in rarest of rare cases, that too, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences.
Article - 21 of the Constitution of India enshrined the detenu the fundamental right of personal liberty which is precious right enshrined to the citizens as per the Constitution of India.
At the same time, duty cast upon the 'State' as KL,J & PSS,J defined under Article - 12 of the Constitution of India to maintain law and order as well as public order.
When there is disturbance to the public order, it is the duty of the 'State' to invoke the procedure laid down under the Act No.1 of 1986, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences.
18. In Vijay Kumar1 the detention order was passed when the detenu was in Jail.

Considering the said facts, the Apex Court held that though the detenu is in Jail, the impugned detention order can be passed relying on the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering the nature of offences and manner in which it was committed.
19. In Smt. K. Aruna Kumari2, the Apex Court held that this Court cannot examine probative value of evidence available to the detaining authority.
20. As discussed above, the facts of the present case would reveal that the detenu is having criminal history and several cases are pending against him.
In all the aforesaid cases, the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious in nature.
Even in Crime No.428 of 2022 of KPHB Police Station, the detenu while committing the offence of chain snatching made an attempt to kill the victim.

Therefore, the facts of the KL,J & PSS,J present case are different to the facts of the case in Mallada K. Sri Ram5, wherein only two (02) crimes were registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under Sections - 420, 468, 471 and 506 read with 120B of IPC and, therefore, the Apex Court considering the same and that the detenu was granted bail on imposition of certain conditions, and there was no disturbance to the public order, set aside the detention order.
21.

The contention of learned Special Government Pleader that keeping in view the past history of the detenu about his involvement in 75 crimes of different Police Stations of different States and that there is every possibility of the detenu committing similar offences in future, the detaining authority passed the impugned order of detention to prevent the detenu from committing similar offence is sustainable.
22.
As discussed above, in the present case, the allegation levelled against the detenu are very serious.

Therefore, viewed from any angle, according to this Court, there is no error in the impugned detention order dated 15.10.2022 passed by respondent No.2 and as confirmed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt. Nos.2247, dated 01.12.2022.
Thus, the writ petition fails and the same is liable to be dismissed.
KL,J & PSS,J 23.
The present writ petition is accordingly dismissed.
In the circumstances of the cases, there shall be no order as to costs.
